_fixture_note: SYNTHETIC clean brief for the L8 judge harness. Mirrors the strategist_briefs row shape (strategic_read + slimmed stories/theory). Every numeric claim traces to a cited source (including normalization cases: '€3.2 billion' vs '3.2bn', '90%' vs '90 percent'); all S#/T# resolve; every falsifier is dated with a threshold; no overclaims.

strategic_read.bottom_line: Leading-edge compute supply, not model quality, now governs AI value capture [S1].

signals.title: TSMC 2nm ramp entrenches foundry concentration
signals.implication: TSMC expanding 2nm capacity to 60,000 wafers per month [S1] while Apple and Nvidia pre-book 90% of that output [S2] evidences the Teece pattern [T1]: the scarce co-specialized asset is leading-edge fabrication, not chip design.
signals.action_rationale: portfolio exposure to a single leading-edge supplier concentrates risk
signals.value_capture: The complementary-asset owner (TSMC) captures value over designers; appropriability upstream is weak.
signals.falsifier: Samsung or Intel wins more than 20% of 2nm-class orders by Q2 2027

signals.title: EU battery subsidy targets a scale externality
signals.implication: The €3.2 billion EU battery manufacturing fund [S3] is industrial policy aimed at a positive externality (domestic cell scale), not antitrust; it lowers the cost side of the chasm for European pragmatist buyers.
signals.action_rationale: co-invest alongside subsidized capacity rather than compete with it
signals.falsifier: Fewer than 2 subsidized gigafactories reach volume production by end of 2028

signals.title: Staged robotics bet is an option, not a commitment
signals.implication: The $500 million humanoid-robotics round [S4] is tranche-staged against deployment milestones — a real option buying information under uncertainty [T2], not a conviction bet on near-term diffusion.
signals.action_rationale: let the option holders pay for the information; enter on milestone evidence
signals.falsifier: Follow-on tranche is cancelled or cut below $200 million by Q1 2027

convergence.theme: Compute supply as the binding constraint
convergence.implication: Chips capacity and AI demand stories point at the same bottleneck.

scenarios.base: Foundry concentration persists; value accrues to fab and energy asset owners through 2027.
scenarios.bull: Subsidized EU capacity lands on time, easing cell supply and accelerating EV diffusion.
scenarios.bear: A capacity glut or export-control shock strands leading-edge capex.

watch.why: would falsify the single-supplier concentration read
confirms whether the subsidy reaches cell makers or diffuses into R&D grants

stories.label: S1
stories.title: TSMC to expand 2nm capacity
stories.summary: TSMC said it will expand 2nm capacity to 60,000 wafers per month by late 2026 across its Hsinchu and Kaohsiung fabs, citing sustained AI accelerator demand.
stories.lens_rationale: capacity scaling on a locked process node

stories.label: S2
stories.title: Apple and Nvidia pre-book most of TSMC's 2nm output
stories.summary: Supply-chain checks indicate Apple and Nvidia have pre-booked 90 percent of TSMC's initial 2nm output, leaving little capacity for other designers.

stories.label: S3
stories.title: EU approves battery manufacturing fund
stories.summary: The European Commission approved a 3.2bn euro fund to subsidize domestic battery cell manufacturing, aiming at gigafactory scale-up through 2028.

stories.label: S4
stories.title: Humanoid robotics startup raises staged round
stories.summary: A humanoid robotics startup raised a $500 million round released in tranches tied to factory-deployment milestones, with the first tranche at $150 million.

theory.label: T1
theory.chunk_text: When imitation is easy (weak appropriability), profits flow to the owners of scarce co-specialized complementary assets — manufacturing, distribution — rather than to the innovator.

theory.label: T2
theory.chunk_text: Staged investment under uncertainty is best valued as a real option: each tranche buys information and the right, not the obligation, to continue.
